title: A Parker wind model moves charged ice across a thin Gaia20cdd dust layer in days
abstract: We test magnetic transport of the small ice grains proposed for Gaia20cdd. A three-dimensional Parker wind model moves a 0.1 um ice sphere at +5 V across one stellar radius in 5.782 days at 3 au for a radial field of 3 nT at 1 au and a 27-day stellar rotation period. These are test inputs, not measured source properties. A local vertical model limits the field to 0.00441 nT if the same charged grain must stay within one stellar radius for 152 days. The full orbit confirms this limit. Alternating field sectors can reduce the motion, but the result depends on reversal time and launch phase. We provide size, radius, radiation-pressure and wind-speed tests. This adds a charge-field condition to thin-screen models that permit cold ice near warm dust. It does not measure a field, grain lifetime or dust supply, and does not refute the ice band. Broad clouds, low charge, gas coupling, current sheets and new grain supply remain open. The package contains original code, aggregate results, checks and source provenance.

display.caption: Conditional magnetic motion of ice grains at 3 au. Constant-polarity crossings and a separate local sector model show the role of size, field and reversal time. Fields and charges are test inputs, not measurements.
